tips.title: Proper Scribing with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. Choose the right size (0.2mm, 0.3mm, or 0.5mm) based on your model's scale. Apply gentle pressure while scribing along the panel line, never force it. For deep lines, use multiple passes. Avoid pressing too hard to prevent damaging the detail.

tips.title: Bending Photo-Etch with Eduard Jigs
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch bending jigs are invaluable for shaping tiny details. Soak the part in warm water for 30 seconds to make it pliable. Place it in the jig and gently bend it using tweezers. Once bent, let it dry naturally to retain its shape. For complex bends, use multiple jigs progressively.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush performing optimally with regular needle cleaning. After each use, disassemble the nozzle and needle. Clean the needle under running water, gently rubbing off dried paint with a soft brush. Use Iwata Airbrush Cleaner for stubborn deposits. Dry and lubricate the needle with Iwata Airbrush Oil before reassembling.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: For precision masking, use Tamiya Low Tack Masking Tape for curved surfaces and fine details. For larger, straighter areas, opt for Kabuki US1 Tape due to its superior adhesion. Always apply tape on a firm, flat surface to prevent creases. To remove, pull it off slowly at a 45° angle to prevent paint from peeling off.

tips.title: Progressive Sanding with ICM Sanding Sticks
tips.text: ICM Sanding Sticks help you achieve a smooth finish on your models. Start with 1500 grit for general smoothing, followed by 2000 grit for removing scratches, and finish with 3000 grit for a mirror-like surface. Wet sand in a circular motion, using a guidance tool like a rubber eraser for straight lines. Rinse and dry between grits to prevent cross-contamination.
